minutes.headline: ZBA approved a peer review engineer for the revised Whalom Road 40B apartments; hearing continued to June 25.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard the revised 40B rental apartment proposal and questioned the developer and civil engineer on parking, drainage, sidewalks, sewer and buffers. The board voted to accept the peer review proposal from Hamway Engineering and agreed a schedule for the waiver list and review. The hearing was continued to June 25.

votes.motion: Approve Hamway's proposal as peer review engineer, as presented.
Set the dates for the waiver list and review, with the board report on the 18th.
Continue the hearing to June 25 at 7:00.

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant said he had already submitted the check for the peer review. It was suggested the check go to the town instead.
Lisa gave the account balance and said it needs replenishing.
The applicant said a gift of recreation equipment goes to the town on the parcel.
The applicant said garages are extra rent per month.
The board discussed whether fees apply as of the original application or today. The Sewer Commission said it retracted its waiver of privilege fees.

decisions.decision: The board asked the peer reviewer to look at sewer fees and report to the Sewer Commission chair; the fee basis is an open item.
The waiver list goes to the peer reviewer within a week, and his review goes to the board by June 18, ahead of the June 25 hearing.
The water district land donation is to be discussed offline, and the town attorney will draft a condition for the decision.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to accept Hamway Engineering's proposal as peer review engineer for the revised Whalom Road 40B rental apartments.
The waiver list goes to the peer reviewer within a week, and his review is due to the board by June 18; the vote setting these dates was not audible.
The board asked the peer reviewer to look at sewer fees; whether fees apply as of the original application or today is still open.
The water district land donation is to be discussed offline, and the town attorney will draft a condition for the decision.
The hearing was continued to June 25 after questions to the developer and civil engineer on parking, drainage, sidewalks, sewer and buffers.

why_it_matters: An independent engineer reviewing the 40B plans and waiver list affects what drainage, sewer and sidewalk conditions the town can attach to a project that can override local zoning.
Sewer connection and privilege fees are unsettled, which bears on what the town's sewer system collects from the development and who covers the cost.
